children: Libya's state energy major, National Oil Corporation (NOC), is reportedly assessing a rehabilitation tender for the onshore Dahra oil field as the country seeks to upgrade ageing oil infrastructure, restore production capacity and increase national crude output towards its target of 2mn barrels per day (bpd),
The redevelopment has previously been valued at $1bn, although the figure represents an earlier project estimate rather than a confirmed contract award or approved investment commitment.

, NOC Chairman Masoud Suleiman discussed the proposed tender with Audit Bureau Chairman Khaled Shakshak on November 15. Earlier development plans envisaged increasing combined production from Dahra and the neighbouring PL6 field to 130,000 bpd. US oilfield services company Halliburton
was previously involved in front-end engineering and design work.

confirmed during a technical meeting with the NOC on November 16 that it was preparing to drill its first exploration well at the Marwa prospect in Contract Area 103/3 (NC74B) by the end of November, targeting a depth of approximately 6,500 feet.

The meeting also reviewed exploration activities undertaken in 2026, proposed programmes for 2027, and outstanding contractual commitments related to seismic surveys and exploratory drilling. The developments follow discussions on November 11 between the NOC and a consortium comprising Spain's Repsol
, Turkey's TPAO and Hungary's MOL regarding exploration programmes scheduled for the second quarter of 2027.
While OMV's drilling preparations signal continued international interest in Libya's upstream sector, the formal launch of the Dahra redevelopment tender has yet to be confirmed.

title: Libya considers Dahra oil field rehabilitation as OMV advances exploration programme
